newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber trade thin, looks for direction.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber trade thin, looks for direction.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was thin by midsession on Monday with some light buying seen for RSS3 grade rubber as players looked for direction in the afternoon session, dealers said.
"I think we saw one trade for 50 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber done, but there wasn't really much activity this morning," a trader said.
"I did not see any of the big players in. People are waiting for some leads from the Japanese markets. Activity was thin early on," another trader said.

One dealer said the market may look for leads later in the week from talks between Thai and Chinese officials on a rubber deal under which Beijing will buy 382,000 tonnes of rubber this year. "Any news there may have a short-term impact on the market," a trader said.
At 0430 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 109.50 U.S. cents a kg from 108.50 cents.

June RSS1 was indicated 154.00-156.00 Singapore cents (US$1.07-$1.08) a kg from 156.25 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 151.00-153.00 Singapore cents (US$1.04-$1.06) a kg from 150.00 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.44) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
